panels.description: The battery's own verdict: OK, WARNING or FAULT, from the fault and warning bit counts the daily health tier reads. This is a prompt to open Battery Health and read the raw fault table, not a diagnosis -- which bit means what is undocumented. Warnings do not outrank faults and do not hide them: a pack showing both reads FAULT. Ignores the time picker.
panels.title: Battery

panels.description: The one tile. DISPATCHING means the loop is alive, serving a fresh plan and writing. It stays green through 'hold' and 'self', which are decisions like any other and are most of a normal day - a tile that demanded an active command would be red by lunchtime and you would stop reading it. Red means the loop is trying and failing: BLIND is a Modbus read it could not do, NOT LANDING is a write the inverter took and did not honour. STALE PLAN means it is fine but flying on old information and will drop to idle. DRY RUN means it is deciding and writing nothing, on purpose. NO DISPATCHER means no point has arrived in five minutes: open the Dispatch dashboard, which has 'Last tick' and 'Why'.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "live" or r._field == "read_error"
                    or r._field == "verified" or r._field == "plan_run")
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.live)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, _value:
      if exists r.read_error then "BLIND"
      else if exists r.verified and r.verified == 0 then "NOT LANDING"
      else if not exists r.plan_run then "NO PLAN"
      else if float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: time(v: r.plan_run))) / 1000000000.0 > 14400.0
        then "STALE PLAN"
      else if r.live == 0 then "DRY RUN"
      else "DISPATCHING" }))
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

panels.title: Dispatcher

panels.description: Is collection happening right now? Green while the newest sample is under 5 minutes old, red past that -- the collector's poll loop never exits on failure, so "container up" says nothing. Matches the 'AlphaESS collector data stale' alert exactly. Ignores the time picker: this is always about now.
panels.title: Collector status

panels.description:
The five jobs that run on a schedule rather than a loop: prices, pricing, efficiency, mijnbatterij and the plan score. Each is measured as HOURS PAST THE INTERVAL IT IS ALLOWED, so one number means the same thing for all five and this tile is the worst of them.

A dead nightly job is the quietest failure in the stack -- nothing errors, a chart just stops moving, and the charts it stops moving are on dashboards nobody opens unless already suspicious. Open the 'Nightly jobs' row below to see which one. Ignores the time picker.

targets.query:
nowS = float(v: int(v: now())) / 1000000000.0

// prices: a healthy day-ahead feed is priced INTO THE FUTURE, so the newest point sits
// ahead of now and the age is negative. Allowance 0 -- the moment the newest price is
// behind us, the planner is optimising over a horizon it cannot see.
prices = from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -7d, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "market_price" and r._field == "market_price")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ job: "prices", _time: r._time, _value:
      (nowS - float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0) / 3600.0 - 0.0 }))
  |> keep(columns: ["job", "_time", "_value"])

// pricing and efficiency: computed_at_unix, WHEN THE JOB RAN -- not the row's own
// timestamp, which is the local midnight of the day it describes and is 51h old on a
// healthy system right before the next run. 30h matches the provisioned efficiency
// staleness alert; pricing runs on the same nightly schedule.
pricing = from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -30d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "daily_cost" and r._field == "computed_at_unix")
  |> group()
  |> max()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ job: "pricing", _time: now(), _value:
      (nowS - r._value) / 3600.0 - 30.0 }))
  |> keep(columns: ["job", "_time", "_value"])

efficiency = from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -30d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "daily_energy" and r._field == "computed_at_unix")
  |> group()
  |> max()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ job: "efficiency", _time: now(), _value:
      (nowS - r._value) / 3600.0 - 30.0 }))
  |> keep(columns: ["job", "_time", "_value"])

// mijnbatterij: the last SUCCESSFUL submit. A run that fired and was rejected is not a
// fresh leaderboard entry, so outcome == "ok" rather than any submit at all.
mijnbatterij = from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -30d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "mijnbatterij_submit"
                   and r._field == "submitted" and r.outcome == "ok")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ job: "mijnbatterij", _time: r._time, _value:
      (nowS - float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0) / 3600.0 - 30.0 }))
  |> keep(columns: ["job", "_time", "_value"])

// plan score: report.sh runs at 06:10 for the day that just ended, so a healthy age sits
// between 6 and 30 hours; 32 is where a run did not fire.
score = from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: -30d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan_score" and r._field == "cost_eur_actual")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ job: "plan score", _time: r._time, _value:
      (nowS - float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0) / 3600.0 - 32.0 }))
  |> keep(columns: ["job", "_time", "_value"])

// union() rather than five findColumn() scalars: findColumn raises on an empty result,
// so one job that has never run would take the whole panel down instead of leaving a
// row out of it.
jobs = union(tables: [prices, pricing, efficiency, mijnbatterij, score])
  |> group()

jobs
  |> max()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: now(), _value: r._value }))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> yield(name: "worst job")

panels.title: Nightly jobs

panels.description: Positive is charging, negative is discharging - the opposite of the raw battery_power_w field, which counts discharge as positive. Decimals are left automatic so the value reads as 1.50 kW above a kilowatt and 850 W below it.

targets.query:

  |> range(start: -1h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "power_readings" and r._field == "battery_power_w")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: -r._value }))

panels.title: Battery Power Now

panels.description: The BMS's own SoH figure (0x011B), read daily. Recomputed by the BMS on the order of weeks, so this tile is a slow trend and nothing else -- a day-to-day change here would mean the register, not the battery. No colour ladder: this repo has no basis for where normal degradation ends on this hardware.

from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -3d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "soh_pct")
  |> last()

panels.title: State of health

panels.description: How many fault bits are set across fault1-6 (0x0131-0x013C), counted hourly. Zero is the normal reading and the only good one. Which bit means what is undocumented, so this number is a prompt to read the raw fault/warning table below, not a diagnosis.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -3h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "active_fault_count")
  |> last()

panels.title: Active faults

panels.description: How many warning bits are set across warning1-6 (0x013D-0x0148), counted hourly. Kept apart from the fault count on purpose: warning6 was outside the block this repo read until 2026-09-02, so if it carries a normally-set bit it pins this tile above zero -- and that must not be able to reach the fault tile.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -3h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "active_warning_count")
  |> last()

panels.title: Active warnings

panels.description: The COLDEST cell in the whole battery, across all three packs -- not one pack's average and not a per-pack reading, which these registers cannot provide. Low matters as much as high: a lithium pack below freezing refuses or derates a charge, so a planned overnight charge that quietly under-delivers in January is a question this tile answers. Read with 'Max cell temp' under it - the SPREAD between them is its own signal, a wide gap meaning one pack is working much harder than its neighbours.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "min_cell_temp_c")
  |> last()

panels.title: Min cell temp

panels.description: The HOTTEST cell in the whole battery, across all three packs. This is the one that decides whether the inverter starts derating: a sustained 4.7 kW discharge is also the hardest thermal load the pack sees, so a shortfall that appears only on long sessions is worth checking against this tile before blaming the dispatcher. 'unreadable' is a failed or implausible register read, not a cold battery -- dispatch/registers.py refuses to publish a temperature it cannot vouch for rather than publishing a wrong one.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "max_cell_temp_c")
  |> last()

panels.title: Max cell temp

panels.description: What the PLAN asked for in the slot covering right now, from slot_action. 'no slot' is normal - it means the plan has nothing scheduled for this moment, not that the dispatcher is down. In dry run this is the only one of these four tiles that moves.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "slot_action")
  |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

panels.title: Decision

panels.description: What the loop actually did with that decision. 'command' wrote the block; 'release' handed the battery back to self-consumption; 'idle' wrote nothing at all, which is the fail-safe. READ IT BESIDE 'Decision', because since #109 the two legitimately disagree: a hold whose charge target is already met releases to soak up surplus solar rather than freezing the battery while the sun spills. Decision 'hold' with Doing 'release' is that working, and 'Why', on the Dispatch dashboard, says so.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "decision_kind")
  |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

panels.title: Doing

panels.description: Time left on the dead man's switch. The loop rewrites it every 60 s, so this should sit near five minutes and never fall far; draining toward zero means the loop has stopped refreshing and the inverter is about to revert to self-consumption on its own. A grey 'no command' means nothing is dispatching, which is a normal resting state and the whole of a dry-run day, not a fault.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state"
                   and (r._field == "expires_at" or r._field == "dispatch_active"))
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.expires_at and exists r.dispatch_active
                   and r.dispatch_active != 0)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, _value:
       float(v: r.expires_at) - float(v: int(v: now())) / 1000000000.0 }))
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: if r._value < 0.0 then 0.0 else r._value }))
  |> yield(name: "expires in")

panels.title: Command expires in

panels.description: Time since the newest plan was made. The schedule runs hourly, so orange at 90 minutes means a run did not fire - which is otherwise silent, because a stale plan still renders perfectly well. Red is 2 hours, which is where the dispatcher stops following the plan at all and lets the battery fall back to self-consumption (slots.MAX_PLAN_AGE).

targets.query:
import "array"

newestT = (from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: -14d, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r._field == "soc_wh")
  |> keep(columns: ["plan_run"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "plan_run")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _value: time(v: r._value) }))
  |> max()
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "_value"))[0]

array.from(rows: [{
  _time: now(),
  _value: float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: newestT)) / 1000000000.0
}])
  |> yield(name: "plan age")

panels.title: Plan age

panels.description: The dispatcher's own sentence for this tick, in the words it logs. 'hold at 0 W', 'plan stale (4.2 h)', 'charge downgraded to hold: target 40% not above live SoC 47%'. This is the tile that turns a red verdict into something you can act on, and until the field was published it existed only in the container log.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state" and r._field == "reason")
  |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

panels.title: Why

panels.description: Three lines on the same instant. 'planned' is the plan's SoC at the END of each interval, shifted onto that end so it lines up with a measurement taken there; 'actual' is the last reading in each 5-minute window, not a quarter-hour average, so a battery that stopped mid-slot shows as a flat stretch rather than a gentler slope. Both are drawn straight between points because SoC ramps; the two step lines are the ones that genuinely hold a value. Read the gaps: commanded against planned is a dispatcher problem, actual against commanded is a delivery one. A step-shaped gap of exactly one interval used to be a charting artefact and no longer is.

targets.query:
newest = (from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: -14d, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r._field == "soc_wh")
  |> keep(columns: ["plan_run"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "plan_run")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ tag: r._value, t: time(v: r._value) }))
  |> sort(columns: ["t"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 1)
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "tag"))[0]

from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r.plan_run == newest and r._field == "soc_wh")
  |> timeShift(duration: 15m)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, "planned": r._value / float(v: ${capacity_wh}) * 100.0 }))
  |> yield(name: "planned")

from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "power_readings" and r._field == "soc_percent")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 5m, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, "actual": r._value }))
  |> yield(name: "actual")

newest = (from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: -14d, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r._field == "soc_wh")
  |> keep(columns: ["plan_run"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "plan_run")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ tag: r._value, t: time(v: r._value) }))
  |> sort(columns: ["t"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 1)
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "tag"))[0]

from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r.plan_run == newest and r._field == "reserve_wh")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, "reserve": r._value / float(v: ${capacity_wh}) * 100.0 }))
  |> yield(name: "reserve")

import "internal/debug"

from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_state")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "target_soc_pct" or r._field == "mode"
                    or r._field == "dispatch_active")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, "commanded":
       if r.dispatch_active != 0 and r.mode == 2 then float(v: r.target_soc_pct)
       else debug.null(type: "float") }))
  |> yield(name: "commanded")

panels.title: Planned SoC vs actual SoC

panels.description: What the dispatcher will do next, as blocks - read from the translator's own slots rather than worked out again from the plan. Contiguous intervals with the same action, power and target are already merged into one slot, so a run of fifteen-minute discharges reads as one evening band. The neutral 'horizon end' block is where the plan stops; without it the last band would run to the edge of the panel and a horizon that ends at 22:00 would look like one that never ends.

defaults.noValue: no slots published - has the translator run since #113?

targets.query:
newest = (from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -48h, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_slots" and r._field == "action")
  |> keep(columns: ["plan_run"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "plan_run")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ tag: r._value, t: time(v: r._value) }))
  |> sort(columns: ["t"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 1)
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "tag"))[0]

nowS = float(v: int(v: now())) / 1000000000.0

// The whole of the newest run, elapsed slots included. Each panel narrows it differently.
run = from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -48h, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispatch_slots" and r.plan_run == newest)
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])

bands = run
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, _value: r.action }))
tail = run
  |> tail(n: 1)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: time(v: int(v: r.end_s) * 1000000000),
                       _value: "horizon end" }))

union(tables: [bands, tail])
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> yield(name: "slots")

panels.title: What the dispatcher will do next

panels.description: Time since the last failed poll. Large and rising is the healthy state.
panels.title: Since last failure

panels.description: Polls that raised an error in the last 24 hours. A handful is normal upstream flakiness; a cluster is an outage. Fixed window, not the time picker -- this dashboard's range runs 36 hours into the future for the plan panels, and a count over that is not a number about anything.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -24h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health" and r.event == "failure" and r._field == "failures")
  |> group()
  |> count()
  |> yield(name: "failed_polls")

panels.title: Failed polls (24h)

panels.description:
Heartbeat pushes to Uptime Kuma that could not be delivered in the last 24 hours, BROKEN DOWN BY WHICH PROCESS could not deliver them -- the collector, efficiency, mijnbatterij or dispatch all write here.

Anything above zero means a dead man's switch is dead: the job may be perfectly healthy and Kuma will still page for silence, or worse, sit green while the job is down. Zero means every push landed, which is the only good reading. Fixed 24h window, not the time picker.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: -24h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health"
                   and r.event == "heartbeat_failed" and r._field == "error")
  |> group(columns: ["component"])
  |> count()
  |> yield(name: "heartbeat_failures")

panels.title: Heartbeat pushes failing (24h)

panels.description:

A job that has never run is absent from this table rather than shown as infinitely late.

panels.description: Total euros the battery has saved across every analysed day so far: sum of (no-battery cost - with-battery cost). Fixed all-time range, independent of the time picker. A negative total would mean the battery has cost money net-to-date.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "daily_cost" and r.model_version == "${model_version}" and r._field == "saving")
  |> group()
  |> sum()
  |> yield(name: "total_saving")

panels.title: Total saving to date

panels.description: Sum of the plan's per-interval cost, positive meaning earning. Matches the 'total benefit' line that advise.py prints for the same run.

targets.query:
newest = (from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: -14d, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r._field == "soc_wh")
  |> keep(columns: ["plan_run"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "plan_run")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ tag: r._value, t: time(v: r._value) }))
  |> sort(columns: ["t"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 1)
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "tag"))[0]

from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: -14d, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r.plan_run == newest and r._field == "cost_eur")
  |> group()
  |> sum()
  |> yield(name: "benefit")

panels.title: Planned benefit over horizon

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "power_readings")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "pv_power_w" or r._field == "grid_power_w" or r._field == "load_power_w" or r._field == "battery_power_w")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: if r._field == "battery_power_w" then -r._value else r._value }))

list.definition: capacity_wh from the newest plan point
list.description: Usable battery capacity in Wh, read from the newest `plan` point the planner wrote. The plan stores SoC in Wh and every percentage here divides by this, so it is sourced from the same run rather than kept in step by hand.
list.label: Capacity (Wh)
list.name: capacity_wh
list.query:
from(bucket: "planning")
  |> range(start: -14d, stop: 72h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "plan" and r._field == "capacity_wh")
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_value: r._value, _run: time(v: r.plan_run)}))
  |> sort(columns: ["_run"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 1)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_value: string(v: int(v: r._value))}))

list.description: daily_cost model_version to read. Bump in pricing.py when the model changes; set the same value here so old and new rows are not double-counted. 4 = export price no longer deducts the sourcing markup (3 and earlier under-credited every exported kWh by ~0.01815 €/kWh); 3 = added load_kwh (total house consumption) for the real-€/kWh panels; 2 = price-coverage gate (days are stored only when their prices are complete); 1 = pre-gate rows, kept for comparison.
list.label: Model version
list.name: model_version
